title: Call: Clinic Physician Reports on Lena's Exam

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - EHS Biosafety Office, ext. 5-0142

callee.name: Marcus Tran, CBSP
callee.label: Biosafety Officer (PI and IBC chair Prof. Dennis Okafor conferenced in)

transcript.speaker: BSO
transcript.text: Biosafety, this is Marcus Tran. I have the PI and Prof. Dennis Okafor on the line. Go ahead, Doctor.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Mbeki
transcript.text: Good. I saw Lena at 10:20. She's well. I've documented the exam and taken a baseline, and nothing is indicated today. That matches your protocol's agent information sheet.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Mbeki
transcript.text: I want her back on Thursday at 09:00 for a follow-up. She's not to go back into that room before then. Please make sure her lab understands that, not just her.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Mbeki
transcript.text: For my chart I've written, quote, possible mucous membrane splash to the face and percutaneous injury through the glove, Risk Group 2 material, 09:02 this morning, Lindgren third floor, end quote. Your committee will want that exact wording. This isn't just a broken tube.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Mbeki
transcript.text: Two more things. First, only one of the two cell biology people has come in. The technician told my front desk she wasn't really near it, and she's gone back to her bench on two. I'd like to see her today.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Mbeki
transcript.text: Second, I still don't have the PI's written description of what happened. I can't close my note without it. My last walk-in slot today is 16:15, and we close at 17:00.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Mbeki
transcript.text: So, who's getting the technician over here, and when can I expect the written account?

transcript.speaker: Dr. Mbeki
transcript.text: All right. Send whatever you have to the clinic by email, and call me if the technician says no. I'll want that noted.

voiceStyles.BSO: Calm, measured professional in their 40s, taking notes while talking
voiceStyles.Dr. Mbeki: Experienced occupational physician in her 50s, brisk and precise, friendly but firm, reading the chart wording slowly and deliberately

instructorNote: This puts the clinic's wording ('possible mucous membrane splash … percutaneous injury') on the record as a fact for classification. Check that the BSO logs the visit, the Thursday follow-up and the exact wording in LI-2026-0142 and gets the cell biology technician seen before 16:15 or 17:00. The PI should send a written account today. The IBC chair should record that an overt BL2 exposure means an immediate NIH report, so the 30-day row on the clock board can't stay unless someone records a reason.
